verdicts.reason: The shared `updatecompatibility` macro now emits `--features=rolling-updates` for every rendering (both call sites in update-compatibility.adoc), with no comment or conditional tying it to the preview stage, so it will silently outlive the preview.

printFeatureDisabled() and the test's ENABLE_FEATURE constant and assertion all embed the literal 'rolling-updates', while UpgradeTest.java:115 in the same PR does derive it from Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey(); Feature.getKey() is computed from the enum name so a rename would desynchronise message and assertions.

Grepping the whole quarkus tree, the only exit-code assertion for this command is assertEquals(0, result.exitCode()) in testCompatible; testFeatureNotEnabled and testWrongVersions assert stderr strings only, so neither the renumbered 3 nor the new 4 is pinned anywhere.

26_2_0.adoc exists and 26_1_0.adoc does carry entries for preview features (e.g. OID4VCI), but recent preview features such as user-event-metrics and passkeys have no release-note entry, so the repo genuinely does not settle it; the project's release-note policy, or a companion docs PR, would.

kc.sh runs a build-and-exit pass unless --optimized is given; shouldSkipRebuild compares the *leaf* command name (asCommandLineList last element is 'metadata'/'check', never 'update-compatibility'), so the skip never fires, and requiresReAugmentation compares all build-time options — the newly mandated build-time --features=rolling-updates differs from the persisted config, so the documented read-only command re-augments and persists the flag into the server's build configuration.

RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE really does change 4 -> 3 and the guide documents these codes as the scriptable contract; the breakage risk is limited because the command landed on main only two weeks earlier (588e60e, 2025-01-24) and is unreleased preview, which is why this is Low rather than higher.

The interface holds ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE and RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE next to the new FEATURE_DISABLED, so the new constant breaks the local naming convention and reads as a flag at picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED).
The identical five-line guard is copy-pasted into both run() methods while the shared parent only owns printFeatureDisabled(), so the gate is opt-in for any future subcommand rather than inherited.

parseAndRun calls PropertyMappers.sanitizeDisabledMappers() immediately before cmd.execute(), and that path invokes Environment.getCurrentOrCreateFeatureProfile(), which configures Profile when getInstance() is null — so CURRENT is always set before run(); Profile.configure also puts an entry for every Feature, so the map lookup cannot unbox null either.

createInitialDeployment returns at `if (updateStrategy == null)` before the FeatureSpec block, and upgradeStrategy() feeds null to testCacheMaxCount, which awaits eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus; UpgradeTest does not use the custom image either, so that case really does run the rolling path with rolling-updates off.

The guide tells users to include every configuration option while the macro unconditionally appends a second --features; ConfigArgsConfigSource.parseArguments() does properties.put(key, value) into a HashMap while iterating the arg list, so the appended occurrence wins and the user's own feature set is dropped. (The metadata file itself is version-only today, so the immediate damage is to the effective profile rather than to the stored metadata.)

verdicts.evidence: docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc CAUTION block; operator/src/main (no Profile/ROLLING_UPDATES reference); UpgradeLogicFactory.java:34-43; UpgradeTest.java:102-117
verdicts.reason: A grep of operator/src/main finds no reference to Profile or ROLLING_UPDATES at all; UpgradeLogicFactory branches solely on UpdateSpec.findUpdateStrategy, and the PR's own UpgradeTest null-strategy case runs the flow with the feature unset — so the CAUTION that the Operator 'will fail' is not backed by any code in this change.

Picocli.exit() only calls System.exit when the code is non-zero and the JVM is not in test launch mode, the surrounding run() already used picocli.exit(result.exitCode()) before this PR, and the new code adds the `return` needed for the test-mode path; the claim also stops at a colon with no stated consequence.

The early return for the default (null) strategy does skip the new FeatureSpec setup, which is the accurate part; the null case still reaches the rolling-upgrade assertion today only because the operator has no feature gate, which is exactly the inconsistency worth flagging.

The table describes exit 4 as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible', but the command never performed a check — it printed 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature rolling-updates is not enabled.' and bailed, so the row overstates what the code was determined to be.

Correct that the `<not set>` default path (RecreateOnImageChangeUpgradeLogic) works with the feature off; in fact no operator path checks the feature, so the CAUTION is broader than the implementation in every branch, not just the default one.

testFeatureNotEnabled launches only {update-compatibility, metadata}; every invocation of the check subcommand in the class passes ENABLE_FEATURE, so the copy of the guard in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() is never exercised in the disabled state.
Same fact as the macro-staleness point: updatecompatibility is the single generic template for both documented invocations and now carries a preview-only flag with nothing marking it temporary.

The renumbering is real and the only explanation added is a comment about picocli's reserved codes; 26_2_0.adoc has no entry for the tool or the exit-code change. Severity stays Low because the command is unreleased preview, so no shipped script depends on the old numbering yet.
